source_ref: Miedema SS, Cheong YF, Naved RT, Yount KM (2023) PLOS ONE 18(10):e0287963, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0287963 (CC BY 4.0); S1 Dataset journal.pone.0287963.s001 (Stata .dta release 118) variable labels (item text) and value labels (options); Table 1 / Table 2 images (.t001/.t002) for completing 20 truncated labels; data/miedema_2023_ecs40.py
note: MAPPING: data_labels, exempt derivation -- data/miedema_2023_ecs40.py melts the S1 .dta columns matching ^ecoscale_\d+$ under var_name='item', so each IRW code IS the source column name; item text is that column's Stata variable label (40/40 read). WORDS: the .dta labels are bilingual English-then-Bangla strings truncated at Stata's 80-char cap, so only 4 (ecoscale_7, 17, 21, 25) carry a complete English question, and the Bangla item wording is cut off entirely for every item. 19 items (ecoscale_1,4,5,6,9,11,14,20,22,23,24,26,28,30,35,36,38,51,56) are completed by appending the tail of the matching ECS-20 'Item Label' in the paper's Table 1 (PNG t001, identical wording in Table 2 t002; transcribed from the image, spot-check advised) after the label's own verbatim prefix, each label prefix matching exactly one Table 1 label; a closing '?' was added to these to match the label style of the complete labels. Label spelling kept where it differs from the table (ecoscale_11 'shouldnt'); ecoscale_26's tail keeps Table 1's 'letting you spent it' although the paper's Results text once writes 'spend'. The remaining 17 items (ecoscale_8, 10, 12, 13, 16, 18, 19, 27, 29, 31, 33, 43, 45, 46, 47, 49, 50) ship the truncated 80-char English label verbatim, unpadded, mid-word where the cap fell; their completions exist only in the ECS-36 paper (Yount et al. 2021, J Interpers Violence, doi:10.1177/0886260520987812), which is closed access (OpenAlex oa_status=closed, no PMC/Europe PMC copy) and was not read. LANGUAGE: administered in Bangla (Bengali) in rural Matlab; no complete Bangla item wording in the deposit (S1 .dta is the only data file; S2 is the inclusivity DOCX), so English is shipped in item_text under the fallback (translated_substitute, study_supplied English from the study's own labels/paper), item_text_translated left empty. option_text holds the administered Bangla from the .dta value labels ('হ্যাঁ'/'না'), with the labels' own English 'Yes'/'No' in option_text_translated; resp 1=Yes/0=No per the processing script's recode (Refused dropped). CORROBORATION (not required, code derivation exempt): the paper's quoted lifetime prevalences match the labelled columns in the .dta -- lowest 2% 'pressured into earning money' = ecoscale_45 1.94%, highest 26% 'women should not work outside the home' = ecoscale_11 25.70%, 'pawned or sold' 2.69% = ecoscale_51 2.69%, 'fear the consequences if you asked him for money' 12.59% = ecoscale_20 12.58%. RIGHTS: ECS is the authors' own scale (paper: 'Our same project team conducted validation of the original ECS-36 questionnaire'); paper and deposit CC BY 4.0; no restriction on the wording located, not in instrument_rights_register.csv. instructions left blank: no literal interviewer instruction is published.
public_note: 17 of the 40 item texts (ecoscale_8, 10, 12, 13, 16, 18, 19, 27, 29, 31, 33, 43, 45, 46, 47, 49, 50) are cut off mid-sentence because the study's data file truncates its question labels at 80 characters and the full wording is published only in a closed-access paper; all item text is the study's English rendering of a Bangla interview.
